director.chapterArc: A progression from physical exertion through tactical drills into a series of character revelations regarding hidden abilities (Milo's light), internal failures (Toren's Ember thinning), and existential crisis (Dessa's obsolescence). The tone shifts from the flat efficiency of survival to the quiet, heavy realization that their individual strengths are liabilities or insufficient.
director.restraintNote: Maintain a grounded, observational distance. Do not dramatize Milo's light as 'magical' but as a cold physical fact. Keep Rook's delivery dry and instructional even when discussing emotional topics like Dessa's future. The horror of Toren's failure is in the thinning attention, not a struggle.

cues.delivery: Shift to instructional rhythm. The narrator is describing a change in methodology; the voice should be precise and slightly detached as it outlines the new drills.
cues.from: Here is how the drilling changed.
cues.through: Toren noticed it and put it away somewhere without knowing why.
cues.reason: Transition from narrative summary of travel into specific tactical instruction.

cues.delivery: Maintain a flat, observational tone for Rook's dialogue. The revelation of Milo's light should be delivered with clinical precision, not wonder. When Milo expresses his hatred for the ability, keep it factual and weary.
cues.through: "There isn't anything nicer," Rook said. "There's just what it does and what it costs. Water, please."
cues.reason: The scene requires a shift from general observation to specific character interaction regarding hidden powers.

cues.delivery: Narrative voice should slow slightly for Toren's internal observation of Wyck and his own struggle. The description of the Ember thinning requires a measured pace to convey the subtle failure.
cues.from: The Wyck thing happened on the sixth day and took about four seconds, and nobody but Toren would have called it anything at all.
cues.through: Fourteen, which felt like a victory until he tried for fifteen and got seven.
cues.reason: Focus on Toren's internal state during the drill.

cues.delivery: Dessa's speech must be delivered with a flat, exhausted intensity. The subtext is not anger but the crushing weight of obsolescence; avoid rising inflection or emotional outbursts.
cues.through: Wyck got a crate under her before Toren had finished turning round.
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional restraint and clarity.

cues.delivery: Rook's final interaction with Dessa is quiet and deliberate. The narrator should maintain a steady cadence as Rook reveals the strap; this is a moment of heavy implication rather than action.
cues.from: Rook came to her that evening after the food, when the fire was down and Milo was doing the water and Toren was pretending to check a strap on the cart's near side, four feet away, where he could hear everything.
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional restraint.

pauses.reason: Emphasis on the first of two critical reasons for moving.

pauses.after: They went north before anybody had eaten, on a drove road with a drainage ditch on one hand and a dead poplar every thirty yards on the other, and it took Toren about half a mile to understand that his shoulders had been given a job this morning so that his mouth would have less to do.
pauses.reason: Completed thought on Toren's realization about his shoulders; allows the listener to absorb the shift in focus.

pauses.after: "Nobody's holding it. I want something to squeeze that isn't the blanket, and your hand is closer than the blanket." A pause. "There. Now we're both being helped and neither of us has to say so."
pauses.reason: End of Senna and Dessa exchange; a moment of shared understanding that requires space before Toren's observation.

pauses.after: "Because I did it last night and there is a cost and it isn't mine." Rook folded the blanket back down. "She's got a bone that has to knit and a body that has to do the knitting. I can hold a door shut for an hour. I can't build the wall."
pauses.reason: Major revelation regarding Rook's limitation ('I can't build the wall'); needs a significant landing for the weight of this admission.
Critical distinction in Rook's capabilities; isolates his limitation.

pauses.after: It fell apart in nine seconds. Wyck went for Milo's shoulders and Toren went for the same shoulders from the other side and they got in each other's way, and by the time they had sorted it out they were standing in a knot of three people inside a yard of ground, which was the exact single thing they had spent two days at the sheep-fold learning not to be.
pauses.reason: End of the failed drill description; pause to let the failure sink in before Rook's correction.
Sets up the tactical definition of a casualty in this world.

pauses.after: Toren noticed it and put it away somewhere without knowing why.
pauses.reason: Brief breath after Toren notices his own improvement without understanding why.

pauses.before: She was better at it than anybody expected
pauses.reason: Highlights Dessa's unexpected competence as a fact of the world.

pauses.before: So we'll stop calling it nothing
pauses.reason: Rook validates Milo's ability; isolates this shift in perspective.
Sets the tone for Rook's question; emphasizes his emotional distance.

pauses.after: "I hate this," Milo said. "That's the whole of it. I've had it since I was thirteen and I hate it and I've never once been glad of it, and now everybody knows."
pauses.reason: End of Milo's outburst; pause to let the raw emotion settle before Rook's response.

pauses.after: "It's a liability," he said. "You're right. Out here, at night, that thing is a beacon and it will get somebody killed, and the fact that you worked that out for yourself at thirteen with nobody to tell you is the only reason I'm not annoyed about the fortnight." He stood up off the wall. "So we're going to treat it as what it is. It goes in the same box as the drag-chain and the water can. It's a tool you own, and it's got a cost, and the cost is everything in the dark knows. You don't use it because you're frightened and you don't use it because it's dark. You use it when the thing you're buying is worth what it costs, and you tell somebody before you do it."
pauses.reason: Rook's full explanation of the light as a liability; this is a key thematic shift requiring time to process.

pauses.before: It goes in the same box as the drag-chain
pauses.reason: Equates a magical ability with mundane tools; isolates this recontextualization.

pauses.after: Then she stopped, because she had to, and stood in the middle of an old sheep road breathing like a woman who has run a mile.
pauses.reason: End of Dessa's physical struggle and her first word 'Right'; pause for the impact of her arrival.
The core of Dessa's grievance; isolates this self-definition as a threat.
Pause after Toren realizes he has no answer to Dessa's question; a moment of collective silence.

pauses.before: Old leather gone soft as cloth
pauses.reason: Descriptive detail emphasizing the age and wear of Rook's strap; isolates this imagery.
Rook's understated answer to Dessa's question about the future; isolates this low-stakes delivery.
